obligations.summary: Providers placing on the market or putting into service AI systems or general-purpose AI models in the Union must comply with this Regulation, regardless of whether they are established inside or outside the Union.
exceptions: AI systems exclusively for military, defence or national security purposes are excluded
AI systems not placed on the market in the Union where output is used exclusively for military, defence or national security purposes are excluded
AI systems or models specifically developed for the sole purpose of scientific research and development are excluded
Research, testing or development activity prior to placing on the market or putting into service is excluded (testing in real-world conditions is not excluded)
AI systems released under free and open-source licences are excluded unless placed on market as high-risk or falling under Article 5 or 50

obligations.summary: Deployers of AI systems with their place of establishment or location within the Union must comply with this Regulation.
exceptions: Deployers who are natural persons using AI systems in the course of a purely personal non-professional activity are excluded
AI systems exclusively for military, defence or national security purposes are excluded
AI systems or models specifically developed for the sole purpose of scientific research and development are excluded

obligations.summary: Providers and deployers of AI systems established or located in a third country must comply with this Regulation where the output produced by the AI system is used in the Union.
exceptions: Public authorities in a third country or international organisations using AI systems under international cooperation or agreements for law enforcement and judicial cooperation with the Union or Member States are excluded, provided adequate safeguards for fundamental rights exist
Output used exclusively for military, defence or national security purposes in the Union is excluded

obligations.summary: Importers and distributors of AI systems must comply with this Regulation.
exceptions: AI systems exclusively for military, defence or national security purposes are excluded
AI systems released under free and open-source licences are excluded unless placed on market as high-risk or falling under Article 5 or 50

obligations.summary: For high-risk AI systems under Article 6(1) related to products covered by Union harmonisation legislation listed in Annex I Section B, only Article 6(1), Articles 102–109, and Article 112 apply, and Article 57 applies only where requirements have been integrated into that harmonisation legislation.

Providers and other actors must ensure that any testing of AI systems in real-world conditions complies with this Regulation, as such testing is not excluded from its scope even where pre-market research and development activities are otherwise exempt.
exceptions: Research, testing or development activity not involving real-world conditions testing and conducted prior to placing on the market or putting into service is excluded

obligations.summary: Providers and deployers must ensure that the processing of personal data in connection with rights and obligations under this Regulation remains subject to and compliant with applicable Union data protection law, including GDPR, Regulation (EU) 2018/1725, Directive 2002/58/EC and Directive (EU) 2016/680.

Providers of AI systems released under free and open-source licences must comply with this Regulation if those systems are placed on the market or put into service as high-risk AI systems or as AI systems falling under Article 5 or Article 50.
exceptions: AI systems released under free and open-source licences that are not placed on the market as high-risk or do not fall under Article 5 or 50 are excluded from the Regulation
